title: Herzog Tasks Eisenkot With Forming Israel's Next Government, a Gunman Kills Six in Kraków, and Paraguay Charges Ex-President Peña Over a Banking Collapse
subhead: Ten days after Israel's inconclusive October 27 election, President Isaac Herzog handed the coalition mandate to former military chief Gadi Eisenkot with the backing of 67 Knesset members, putting Benjamin Netanyahu closer to the opposition benches than at any point in recent years. In Europe, a far-right-linked shooting in central Kraków killed six people as France faced another weekend of cost-of-living clashes and foreign-linked aviation bomb threats, while in South America a systemic banking failure brought criminal charges against Paraguay's ousted president.

sections.heading: Herzog Gives Eisenkot 28 Days to Replace Netanyahu
sections.body:
Israeli President Isaac Herzog announced on Saturday evening that he will formally task Gadi Eisenkot, leader of the opposition Yashar party and former Israel Defense Forces chief of staff, with forming the next government on Sunday (Reuters, AP News, Anadolu Agency). Following post-election consultations after the deadlocked October 27 vote, Eisenkot secured recommendations from 67 lawmakers in the 120-seat Knesset, according to Israeli media reports cited by Dünya and The Guardian.

Under Israeli law, Eisenkot will have 28 days to assemble a governing coalition, with the president holding discretion to grant an extension of up to 14 additional days (Washington Post, Axios). Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's right-wing bloc lost its parliamentary majority in last month's election, leaving the anti-Netanyahu alliance with the arithmetic to govern if it can bridge internal ideological divides (DW, New York Times).

The mandate arrives at a sensitive moment for Israeli defense planning. Analysts cited by Breaking Defense warned this week that potential post-midterm reductions or conditions on US military assistance could directly affect Israeli acquisition timelines for Apache helicopters, F-15 and F-35 fighter jets, and precision munitions. Meanwhile, the Arab Joint List warned on Saturday that winter flooding in Gaza has swamped 70,000 tents housing displaced Palestinians entering their fourth winter in temporary shelters (Anadolu Agency).
sections.whyItMatters: A 67-seat recommendation gives Eisenkot a mathematical majority on paper, but holding together a broad anti-Netanyahu coalition will test whether opposition parties can agree on wartime budgets, judicial policy, and relations with a Democratic-controlled US Congress.

sections.heading: Six Killed in Kraków Attack as European Security Pressures Mount
sections.body:
At least six people — four women and two men — were killed and around 15 others injured on Saturday afternoon when a gunman dressed in military fatigues drove onto the historic Main Square in Kraków, Poland's second-largest city, and opened fire at random from his vehicle (Reuters, BBC, CBS News). Polish police shot and wounded the suspect, who was taken to a hospital under guard (New York Times).

Prime Minister Donald Tusk traveled immediately to Kraków as investigators examined the suspect's background, with a government minister telling reporters that preliminary findings suggest the attacker was influenced by far-right ideology (The Guardian, The Independent). US Ambassador to Poland Tom Rose also issued a statement condemning the attack.

Across Western Europe, internal security services faced simultaneous strain on Saturday. In France, police used tear gas, batons, and water cannons against cost-of-living and student demonstrators in several cities even as overall turnout dipped from previous weeks, while French prosecutors opened an investigation into suspected foreign-power links behind a wave of false bomb threats targeting commercial aircraft (DW, New York Times, Anadolu Agency). In Latvia, farmers blocked roads to protest the transit of Russian 'blood grain' through Baltic ports, and in Tirana, Albanian police deployed water cannons against masked protesters blocking central thoroughfares (Al Jazeera).
sections.whyItMatters: European interior ministries are contending with three overlapping pressures at once: domestic political violence, sustained street protests over living costs, and hybrid aviation disruptions that French prosecutors now explicitly suspect of foreign state sponsorship.

sections.heading: Post-Midterm Fallout in Washington and the Erdoğan-Trump Call
sections.body:
Days after Democrats won control of Congress in Tuesday's midterm elections — a result The Hill attributed in part to voter opposition to the eight-month Iran war and tariff policies — President Donald Trump called on the Department of Justice to investigate Democratic lawmakers who have floated impeachment proceedings against Republican cabinet officials, describing the talk on Truth Social as 'extortion at the highest level' (The Hill, Al Jazeera). On the Democratic side, an online petition opposing Hakeem Jeffries for House Speaker surpassed one million signatures, calling for a competitive floor vote, while newly elected Michigan Senator Abdul El-Sayed launched a new political action committee named 'Habibi PAC' (Anadolu Agency).

On the diplomatic front, Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan spoke by phone with Trump on Saturday to discuss bilateral relations, the US-Iran conflict, and the Russia-Ukraine war, emphasizing diplomacy to end both conflicts (Dünya, Bloomberg HT). Erdoğan also confirmed he will travel to Karabakh on Sunday at the invitation of Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev to mark Azerbaijan's Victory Day (Independent Türkçe, Habertürk).

In Tehran, senior security officials warned of a 'devastating response' if Washington initiates a new round of strikes, while IRGC spokesman Hossein Mohebbi stated that Iran is actively working to extend the range of its missile arsenal (Anadolu Agency, Habertürk). Iranian state agency IRNA separately reported two explosions heard on Qeshm Island near the Strait of Hormuz and in Jask (Anadolu Agency, Milliyet).
sections.whyItMatters: An incoming Democratic Congress narrows the White House's domestic room for an open-ended Middle East campaign just as Ankara steps up direct leader-to-leader outreach between Washington and regional capitals.

sections.heading: Yemen's Front Line Shifts on the Ground While Red Sea Toll Emails Continue
sections.body:
Fighting inside Yemen intensified on Saturday as internationally recognized government forces reported ground advances and 875 operations neutralizing 130 Houthi fighters, while Houthi-run Al-Masirah television reported that coalition airstrikes on the village of Al-Shariyah in Sanaa's Bani Hashish district killed at least 25 to 27 people (Al Jazeera, Anadolu Agency).

At sea, an investigation by the Wall Street Journal detailed how commercial shipping companies continue to navigate the Red Sea corridor by emailing Houthi authorities directly to secure passage clearances. Further north, Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi ordered the cancellation of contracts with three companies operating at Mosul International Airport after intelligence assessments linked the firms to armed factions, directing that airport operations be transferred to international contractors (Star, Arab News).

In the South Caucasus, Armenian Security Council Secretary Alen Simonyan publicly criticized Yerevan's decades-long reliance on Russian security guarantees, stating that normalizing relations with Turkey is essential and that Russia's military base would not protect Armenia in a crisis (Star).
sections.whyItMatters: Baghdad's removal of militia-linked firms from Mosul Airport and Yerevan's public pivot toward Ankara show smaller regional states actively reducing their exposure to weakened external patrons.

sections.heading: Paraguay's Banking Collapse Brings Criminal Charges Against Ex-President Peña
sections.body:
Prosecutors in Paraguay filed formal criminal charges against former President Santiago Peña and requested his preventive detention following a systemic banking collapse that toppled his administration and left millions of citizens unable to access their savings (BBC, Reuters, The Guardian).

The crisis began last week when depositors across the country found bank accounts frozen and digital payment systems offline, triggering rapid political fallout that forced Peña from office (The Guardian). Prosecutors are now investigating the former president's alleged role in regulatory failures and financial transactions preceding the freeze.
sections.whyItMatters: A sovereign banking freeze that removes a sitting president within days sets a stark warning for Latin American financial regulators managing dollar liquidity and domestic bank supervision.

bottomLine: Israel's political deadlock broke toward the opposition on Saturday as President Herzog handed Gadi Eisenkot 28 days and a 67-seat mandate to form a government without Benjamin Netanyahu. In Washington, the political aftermath of Tuesday's midterms is already reshaping foreign policy expectations as President Trump spars with an incoming Democratic Congress while speaking with Turkey's President Erdoğan on Iran and Ukraine. Meanwhile, Europe's internal security agenda tightened after a gunman killed six people in Kraków and French prosecutors linked aviation bomb hoaxes to foreign interference, and in South America, Paraguay's sudden banking collapse moved from presidential ouster to criminal prosecution.
sources: Reuters, AP News, BBC, Al Jazeera, The Guardian, New York Times, Washington Post, Wall Street Journal, Axios, DW, France 24, CBS News, The Hill, The Independent, Anadolu Agency, Breaking Defense, Dünya, Bloomberg HT, Habertürk, Star
